title: House Robber III
summary: Each tree node contains an amount you may collect.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–10000 nodes with values in [0,10000]. Input uses level-order values with null for absent children. Return an integer total.
contractDetails.output-checking: Build TreeNode objects from level-order input and invoke robTree(root). Compare the returned integer optimum.

statement: Each tree node contains an amount you may collect. Choose nodes with the greatest possible total, with the restriction that a node and its direct parent cannot both be chosen. Return that maximum total.

examples.explanation: Either the root or both children achieves the same best total.

constraints: 1–10000 nodes with values in [0,10000]. Input uses level-order values with null for absent children. Return an integer total.
hints: Conceptual: Choosing a node affects its children but does not forbid its grandchildren.
Directional: Keep separate best totals for choosing and skipping each node.
Implementation: Compute children before their parent. Choosing the parent uses the children’s skip totals. Skipping it uses each child’s better total.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(h) active traversal state. Fixed-capacity internal buffers allocate O(Nmax) storage, where Nmax=10000; dynamically growing stacks need O(h).
